newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bankers say Colombian economy still "critical".
newsitem.headline: Bankers say Colombian economy still "critical".

text.p: BOGOTA, April 30 Reuter - The Colombian economy is still in "critical condition" and annual growth in gross domestic product GDP could be as low as 3 percent, an influential bankers' group said in a report Wednesday.

The report by the National Association of Financial Institutions ANIF said the first quarter of this year had been a total "loss" for the economy. It calculated GDP would have to grow by more than 6 percent in the second half of the year if the annual rate was to reach its most optimistic growth forecast of 3.5 percent.
Earlier this week, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo forecast GDP would grow by about 4 percent, compared to the 2.1 percent in 1996.

"The most recent data clearly indicates that in the first few months of 1997 the economy is still in critical situation," ANIF said in its report presented to a business forum in Bogota, attended by Ocampo.

ANIF painted a gloomy picture on the job front, predicting unemployment would increase to more than 14 percent by mid-year. Colombia's January to March urban unemployment figure grew to 12.7 percent, its highest level in nine years, compared to 11.3 percent at the end of last year.
But ANIF also forecast that joblessness would drop back from that mid-year high to about 13.5 percent by the end of the year.
The influential financial organization, frequently critical of the government's economic policy, said the peso exchange rate would continue to pose problems.
Businessmen contend that the peso value of exports was hurt last year when the government failed to devalue the currency by the full targeted amount.
ANIF forecast the nominal devaluation of the peso would be at the lower end of the 15 percent to 29 percent target set by the central bank.
It said there would be a "significant" build-up of foreign reserves and estimated the peso would stand at about 1,160 against the dollar by the end of the year. The peso closed Tuesday at 1,062.95.
